definitions.explanation: A genre of fiction or thought that imagines scientific and technological developments beyond current reality, or the speculative science depicted in such works.

examples.japanese: {空想|くうそう}{科学|かがく}{小説|しょうせつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{好|す}き→好き：02355_suki⟧だ。
⟦かつて→かつて：10303_katsute⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{空想|くうそう}{科学|かがく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{現実|げんじつ}→現実：02720_genjitsu⟧になった⟦{例|れい}→例：09932_rei⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: There are many examples of what was once science fiction becoming reality.

examples.japanese: {空想|くうそう}{科学|かがく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{世界|せかい}→世界：01447_sekai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{人類|じんるい}→人類：01578_jinrui⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{宇宙|うちゅう}→宇宙：01861_uchuu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{自由|じゆう}→自由：01148_jiyuu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{旅|たび}→旅：03407_tabi⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: In the world of science fiction, humanity travels freely through space.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{空想|くうそう}→空想：00256_kuusou⟧ (fantasy; imagination) and ⟦{科学|かがく}→科学：01277_kagaku⟧ (science). Used as a more traditional Japanese term for the science fiction genre. The popular book series {空想|くうそう}{科学|かがく}{読本|どくほん} (by Yanagita Rikao) humorously analyzes the scientific plausibility of anime and manga, making this term widely recognized.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {空想|くうそう}{科学|かがく}{小説|しょうせつ}: science fiction novel
- {空想|くうそう}{科学|かがく}⟦{映画|えいが}→映画：02273_eiga⟧: science fiction film
- {空想|くうそう}{科学|かがく}{読本|どくほん}: science fiction reader (famous book series)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- SF（エスエフ）: science fiction — the most common abbreviation used in Japanese
- サイエンス⟦フィクション→フィクション：11005_fikushon⟧: science fiction — the full loanword, less commonly used
- ⟦{空想|くうそう}→空想：00256_kuusou⟧: fantasy; daydream — the broader concept of imagining things that don't exist
